primary_claim: A software tool using SAE feature vectors to construct 'ghost token' definition trees (via forward passes) and cosine-similarity-based closest-token lists (without forward passes) can produce human-interpretable descriptions of Gemma-2B SAE features, though results are inconsistent and highly sensitive to parameter choices (encoder vs decoder weights, scaling factor, PCA adjustment), succeeding clearly on some features and only partially on others.
stated_future_work: Adapt the code to work with SAEs trained on other LLMs
Merge common controls between the definition-tree and token-list functionalities for streamlined interaction
Explore impacts of multiple PCA components and linear combinations of encoder- and decoder-based feature vectors
Export outputs for further interpretation via LLM API, enabling automated analysis
Use feature vectors as steering vectors and/or clamp the relevant feature at high activation to direct the interpretive process (author's top-priority next direction)
limitations_stated: Producing relevant trees or lists often requires parameter experimentation, making automated feature interpretation far from straightforward
Tree generation at scale could be time-consuming and compute-intensive
Not clear why some features require larger scaling factors, or why some are more tractable with decoder-based vs encoder-based feature vectors
quote: A software tool is presented which includes two separate methods to assist in the interpretation of SAE features.
